name: Education
summary: Modern EdTech platforms for smarter learning.
description: Education UI UX design for course platforms, learning apps and LMS tools: lesson flows, progress tracking and dashboards that keep learners coming back.
image_alt: Students learning on laptops, education industry
overview:
Learning products compete with every other app on the phone. A confusing lesson screen or a missing next step is often all it takes for a learner to drift away. My job is to keep the path clear: what to do now, how far they have come and what comes next.

I work with founders and product teams on web and mobile education products, from the first prototype to a design system engineers can build from directly. On Learnly, a course platform built for focus, I reworked the learning flow to reduce drop-off between lessons. I bring that same focus on completion to every project.

challenges.title: Drop-off between lessons
challenges.text: Learners lose momentum when the next step is unclear or the flow breaks between lessons.

challenges.title: Keeping focus
challenges.text: Busy screens, notifications and clutter pull attention away from the actual learning.

challenges.title: Many user roles
challenges.text: Students, teachers, parents and admins all need different views of the same content.

challenges.title: Showing real progress
challenges.text: Progress and results have to feel meaningful, or learners stop caring about them.

faqs.question: Do you have experience designing education products?
faqs.answer: Yes. I designed Learnly, a course platform built for focus, where I reworked the learning flow to reduce drop-off between lessons. You can see it in the case studies on this page.

faqs.question: How do you keep learners engaged without adding distractions?
faqs.answer: I focus on clear next steps, visible progress and calm lesson screens. Reminders and rewards support the learning rather than compete with it.

faqs.question: Can you design for students, teachers and admins in one product?
faqs.answer: Yes. I map each role early, then design separate views that share one design system, so the product stays consistent as it grows.

faqs.question: Do you design for both web and mobile?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many learners switch between devices, so I design responsive web apps and native-feeling iOS and Android screens that share one system.

faqs.question: How do we start?
faqs.answer: Send me a short brief through the contact page. We will have a call about your product, users and timeline, and I will come back with a plan and quote.
